summary: Defines the starting principles and policy for the tpc.int subdomain, a set of service listings reachable over the Internet through a name space within the Domain Name System.

eli5.summary: Think of a directory of special services hidden inside the Internet's address book. This memo sets the first rules for running it.

questions: how does tpc.int map phone numbers to hosts
what is the board of arbitration and conciliation
subtitle: The founding rules for tpc.int, a corner of the DNS that maps telephone numbers to Internet hosts willing to print or fax for you.

tldr.problem: Sites could already run gateways between Internet mail and telephone-connected devices such as fax machines, but each was a single-site, value-added service with no shared namespace.
tldr.mechanism: Sites register DNS MX records in the tpc.int subdomain, keyed by telephone-number prefix, and a cooperative run by a Board of Arbitration and Conciliation sets the policy.
tldr.outcome: The memo is informational and applies only to sites that choose to register. It sets the principles for a remote printing service built on Internet mail, not a standard.

facts.label: Board terms
facts.value: Two years (50 percent or more of the initial Board serve one year)

facts.label: Initial service
facts.value: Remote printing to G3 fax devices

today: RFC 1530 is an Informational memo from October 1993 and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It states that it sets only initial principles, to be amended by the cooperative's membership. The technical and administrative details are in RFC 1528 and RFC 1529.

sections.title: What tpc.int Is For
sections.content:
RFC 1530 defines the initial principles of operation for the tpc.int subdomain, a collection of service listings reachable over the Internet through an administered namespace inside the Domain Name System. Its primary purpose is a transparent mapping between general-purpose Internet computers and special-purpose devices connected directly to the telephone network.

The first service is remote printing. It ties together G3-compatible facsimile devices with users of electronic mail in the Internet and in message-handling domains connected to it through application-layer gateways. The memo points out that remote printer gateways were already technically feasible; what tpc.int adds is a common namespace that turns a single-site service into a transparent one.
sections.eli5: It is a way to reach machines on the phone network, like fax machines, from the Internet without knowing who runs the connection.

sections.title: Services Built on Internet Mail
sections.content:
The remote printing facility sits on top of Internet electronic mail, including the message format of RFC 822 and MIME. Because it uses ordinary message handling, the service is also open to systems behind application-layer gateways, such as X.400 systems, UUCP-based environments and commercial mail services like MCI Mail and CompuServe.

The subdomain is run as a cooperative: an association that exists to provide the defined service without gain to itself. Its members are the Internet sites that provide access to the services, under terms the membership can amend.

The technical procedures and administrative policies are in the companion memos, RFC 1528 and RFC 1529.
sections.eli5: The service travels as email, so anyone who can send email, even from a different kind of network, can use it.

sections.title: Naming with MX Records
sections.content:
A site that runs a remote printer server registers itself in the DNS with one or more MX records in tpc.int. Each record names the part of the telephone numbering plan the site will serve. For example, a host willing to serve numbers beginning +1-415-336 is listed as *.6.3.3.5.1.4.1.tpc.int. IN MX 10 hewes.radio.com.

The precision is arbitrary. A record for *.5.1.4.1.tpc.int. covers every printer in area code 415, while a record for *.8.6.9.5.1.4.1.tpc.int. covers area code 415, exchange prefix 968. An organization whose printers all share the prefix +1-415-96 could register *.6.9.5.1.4.1.tpc.int.

Administrators of the namespace must register only sites willing to follow the principles of operation. Every site that meets them is to be registered without bias, and the subdomain should encourage as many sites as possible.
sections.eli5: The phone number is written backwards as a web-style address, and the shorter the number prefix, the bigger the area the helper covers.

sections.title: Fair Ordering of Competing Sites
sections.content:
If several sites will serve the same area, several records exist for the same name. The DNS returns them as an unordered list, but in practice the initiator tries them in the order returned.

To keep the environment unbiased, an authoritative name server for tpc.int shall alternate the ordering of the list frequently and shall return a small TTL with the records. This spreads requests across the competing sites rather than favoring whoever is listed first.
sections.eli5: If three shops all offer the same service, the list is shuffled each time so no shop is always first in line.

sections.title: The Board of Arbitration and Conciliation
sections.content:
Policy is set by the Board of Arbitration and Conciliation, made up of members of the cooperative. The name comes from English law, where tradesmen could appoint councils to settle matters that could not otherwise be settled. The Board hears questions between members about the definition or operation of listed services, takes comments from other members and the general public, and publishes a determination of policy.

The initial Board has five named members, from the Netherlands, Japan, Australia and the United States. Members serve two-year terms, except that 50 percent or more of the initial Board serve one-year terms. The Board is to publish procedures for members to choose new Board members as terms expire.

Secretariat services are initially provided by the Internet Multicasting Service, a non-profit corporation in Washington, D.C., and the cooperative may contract with other groups at any time. The memo also encourages other service-listing domains, whether public trusts, cooperatives or purely commercial ventures; sites may register in those as well as, or instead of, tpc.int.
sections.eli5: A small council of members settles arguments and writes the rules, and a non-profit group does the office work.
